market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Which plant milk has the least sugar and fewest calories?

seo.title: Lowest-sugar, lowest-calorie plant milks compared
seo.meta_description: Unsweetened almond, oat and soy milks can differ sharply in calories and protein. Compare current U.S. labels and see why lowest calorie is not the whole story.
seo.search_intent: Find the plant milk lowest in sugar and calories

excerpt: There is no permanent category winner because formulas change, but current U.S. examples show the trade-off clearly: Silk Unsweet Almondmilk has 30 calories and 0 g sugar per cup, Oatly Unsweetened Oatmilk has 40 calories per cup, and Silk Unsweet Soymilk has 80 calories but 8 g protein and less than 1 g sugar. Lowest calorie and most nutritionally similar to milk are different questions.
content_html:
If you only ask which plant milk is lowest in calories, unsweetened almond milk often wins. But the lightest product is not automatically the closest nutritional replacement for dairy milk.

Three current U.S. examples

Per 1 cup (240 mL)Unsweet almondUnsweet oatUnsweet soy
Calories304080
Total sugars0 gCheck current label<1 g
Protein1 gVaries by formula8 g

The almond example is lowest in calories, while soy provides eight times as much protein as that almond milk.

Unsweetened matters more than the plant name

Original, vanilla and barista versions may add sugar or more oil. Two oat milks from the same brand can differ by more than 100 calories per cup. Oatly currently lists 40 calories for Unsweetened and 160 for Full Fat.

Zero sugar does not mean complete nutrition

Silk Unsweet Almondmilk has 0 g sugar and 30 calories, but only 1 g protein. Silk Unsweet Soymilk has less than 1 g sugar and 80 calories but 8 g protein, plus calcium and vitamin D fortification.

What the FDA recommends checking

The FDA advises comparing protein, calcium, vitamin D and potassium as well as added sugars and saturated fat. Fortified soy beverage is the plant alternative currently treated as nutritionally similar enough to milk to sit in the Dairy Group of U.S. dietary guidance.

Bottom line

For the fewest calories among these examples, unsweet almond wins. For a higher-protein milk replacement, unsweet soy is much closer to dairy milk. Choose the actual carton, not the category stereotype.

faq.question: Which plant milk has the fewest calories?
faq.answer: Among the current examples here, Silk Unsweet Almondmilk at 30 calories per cup, versus 40 for Oatly Unsweetened and 80 for Silk Unsweet Soymilk.

faq.question: Which has the least sugar?
faq.answer: Silk Unsweet Almondmilk lists 0 g total sugar; Silk Unsweet Soymilk lists less than 1 g and 0 g added sugar.

faq.question: Is almond milk better because it has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. It has much less protein than soy in these examples: 1 g versus 8 g per cup.

faq.question: What should I check besides sugar?
faq.answer: Protein, calcium, vitamin D, potassium, saturated fat and whether the product is fortified.
